subject: EU data locality, retention and deletion Q&A — Schrems II / SCCs implications
messages:
From: Claire Bianchi <claire.bianchi@helioshealth.eu>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helioshealth.eu>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU only processing requirement and a few questions about deletion flow

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start procurement for our new clinical notes indexing project, our legal team needs to confirm a few things before we can proceed. High level ask: Helios must have EU only processing for all patient data and the contract has to include SCCs per our counsel. Below are our initial questions — can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these and any caveats?

1) Processing locality: is all inference, caching, and control plane metadata stored and processed only in EU regions when configured? Please call out any control plane operations that might touch non-EU infrastructure (telemetry, usage analytics, billing).

2) Logs and telemetry: what types of logs are retained by default, where are they stored, and can retention be limited or disabled for specific customers? We need to ensure audit logs containing patient identifiers can be purged on request.

3) Deletion API: how does the deletion flow work for model inputs, KV cache, and any stored embeddings? Is there a guaranteed SLA for full deletion and a proofable audit trail we can reference?

4) SCCs and legal: does Redwood rely on SCCs alone or do you also offer additional contractual safeguards (e.g., DPA clauses, supplementary measures)? If you rely on SCCs, do you have guidance on which modules remain in scope vs. any cross-border transfers for support or diagnostics?

I've attached our questionnaire spreadsheet with a few finer points. Our counsel at Berg & Co. are copied; they may follow up. Can you get back to us with a short write up and ideally a diagram of where data flows in EU-only mode?

Best,
Claire
Head of Data Governance, Helios Health
attachments: helios-sccs-questions.xlsx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bianchi <claire.bianchi@helioshealth.eu>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T12:08:00Z
Subject: Re: EU only processing requirement and a few questions about deletion flow

Hi Claire,

Thanks for the clear list. We can support an EU-only processing posture for Helios in our Dedicated and Private deployment modes. Quick answers up front, then I will loop in engineering and privacy for details and the diagram.

- Processing locality: inference and KV cache can be pinned to EU regions; the hosted control plane can be configured with a customer-managed private control plane in EU for Private customers. For Hosted customers we provide EU tenancy options and a data residency guarantee in the DPA.

- Logs and telemetry: by default we capture request metadata for billing and SLO observability. We support configurable retention windows per-customer and can disable application-level telemetry on Dedicated/Private. Platform-level operational logs needed for security and SLA diagnostics may be retained but can be scrubbed on request.

- Deletion API: we expose a deletion endpoint that clears stored embeddings, KV entries, and persisted prompts on demand. For in-flight traces and caches there are TTLs and an expedited purge workflow. We can provide an export of deletion events for proof.

- SCCs and legal: we offer a standard DPA that includes SCCs as well as supplementary measures (encryption at rest, customer-managed keys, and logging minimization). I'll ask legal to produce a summary of what is covered by SCCs vs support diagnostics.

Attaching a preliminary data flow diagram and noting the Helios questionnaire. Internal: Jonas and Soojin, can you expand the answers below with exact retention windows, proof-of-deletion steps, and any non-EU control plane caveats? Markus, can you confirm KMS options and whether we can provide customer-managed keys in EU-only control planes?

Next step: internal sync today if possible and I'll send a consolidated response back to Helios by EOD Friday.

Best,
Evelyn
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: EU only processing requirement and a few questions about deletion flow

Evelyn / team,

I pulled together specifics to respond to Helios and to support Berg & Co. counsel. Key points below — will add links to snippets of the DPA and the deletion audit format.

1) Processing locality
- Hosted API: we have EU-region tenancy for data-at-rest and inference, but the control plane that orchestrates routing and billing is multi-region by default. For customers requiring strict EU-only control plane, we offer Private deployment or a VPC-based private control plane that keeps control plane metadata in EU.
- Dedicated: compute and KV storage provisioned in EU only; no cross-border inference.

2) Logs and telemetry
- Default retention: request-level telemetry 90 days; aggregated metrics 2 years.
- Options: retention windows can be reduced to 30/7/0 days depending on contract; for Private we can set to 0 for application telemetry.
- Audit logs that contain PII are stored encrypted in EU and can be purged via deletion workflow. We maintain a deletion ledger (audit) that records deletion events for compliance.

3) Deletion API and SLA
- API endpoints: POST /v1/customers/{id}/delete-data (initiates purge for embeddings, KV, persisted prompts), GET /v1/customers/{id}/deletion-status (returns events).
- SLA: standard deletion completes within 72 hours for persisted artifacts; expedited 24 hours available for Dedicated/Private with contractual commitment.
- Proof: we provide a signed deletion manifest containing resource IDs, timestamps, and hashes; can be delivered as a PDF or via secure Drive link.

4) SCCs and supplementary measures
- We include SCCs in the DPA and apply supplementary measures: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, optional customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) with EU key stewardship, and reduced telemetry.
- Support/diagnostics: some operational diagnostics may be transited to non-EU support when customers opt into global support. For Helios we can restrict diagnostics to EU-only personnel and EU-hosted tools when in Private/EU Dedicated.

Open items for final response to Helios:
- Confirm exact retention windows Helios wants and whether they require 0-days telemetry.
- Confirm whether Helios requires customer-managed keys in-scope.
- Berg & Co.: please advise if the deletion manifest format meets your audit requirements; if not, list required fields.

I will attach a short excerpt from the DPA and a sample deletion manifest after legal signs off.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bianchi <claire.bianchi@helioshealth.eu>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helioshealth.eu>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Berg & Co. Counsel <counsel@bergco.eu>
Date: 2026-06-29T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU data locality, retention and deletion Q&A — next steps and proposed commitments

Hi Claire / Oliver,

Thanks for the patience while we pulled details together. Summary and proposed commitments for Helios:

1) EU processing posture: Redwood will operate inference, KV cache, and persisted embeddings in EU regions only for the Helios deployment. If you select Private or Dedicated, the control plane can be provisioned to keep orchestration metadata and operational dashboards in EU. For hosted deployment with DPA tenancy we will ensure data-at-rest and inference remain in EU but some control plane telemetry may be routed for billing; we will document which telemetry fields are sent and can limit them to non-identifying fields.

2) Retention and telemetry: default request telemetry retention is 90 days, but for Helios we propose a contractually constrained retention of 30 days for request-level telemetry and 365 days for aggregated metrics. If you require stricter settings we can set telemetry retention to 0 for Private.

3) Deletion and proof: we will commit to deletion SLA of 24 hours for persisted artifacts (embeddings, KV, persisted prompts) for Dedicated/Private customers in the contract. We will provide a signed deletion manifest (resource ids, timestamps, hashes) and an API endpoint to view deletion status.

4) SCCs and supplementary measures: we will include SCCs in the DPA and apply supplementary measures including customer-managed KMS keys in EU (if elected), minimized telemetry, and EU-only diagnostics for support. Any cross-border transfers tied to global support will be explicitly documented and require prior consent.

Next actions:
- Berg & Co., can you confirm the deletion manifest fields required or accept the sample we will produce?
- Helios, please confirm whether you prefer Private or Dedicated control plane so we can include exact language and KMS options in the SOW.
- I will schedule a short call next week with engineering and privacy to walk through the diagram and answer any follow-ups. Proposed time slot: Tue 7/7 10:00 CET.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to run through specifics.

Best,
Evelyn
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
